vignette: Ahmed, a 34-year-old Middle Eastern man, works as a publisher in the bustling city center. His days are filled with managing deadlines and editing manuscripts, but lately, his focus has been waning due to an overwhelming sense of anxiety and a constant fear that something terrible is about to happen again. The trauma began three years ago when Ahmed’s younger brother was involved in a car accident while visiting from their home country. The images of the shattered vehicle and the paramedics rushing around him are still vivid in his mind, replaying whenever he closes his eyes or during moments of quiet contemplation at work. At first, Ahmed tried to push these thoughts away, but they crept back in with a vengeance. Ahmed's wife, Aisha, has noticed changes in her husband over the past few months. He has become distant and irritable, often snapping at her for minor things. The once-enthusiastic planner of their family gatherings now avoids social events altogether. "I just can't handle being around a lot of people right now," he tells Aisha. Ahmed feels suffocated in crowded spaces, where the cacophony of voices and movement trigger flashbacks to that chaotic scene at the accident site. At work, Ahmed struggles to concentrate on tasks that once came easily. He finds himself zoning out during meetings, his mind wandering back to the day his brother was injured. The sound of a car alarm can suddenly freeze him in his tracks, jolting him into a state of high alert. His colleagues have observed this behavior with concern but haven't fully understood its cause. Recently, Ahmed has begun experiencing severe nightmares where he relives the moment his brother’s car was hit, over and over again. In these dreams, he is helpless to stop it from happening, which leaves him drenched in sweat and shaking when he wakes up. The nightmares have made sleep a rare luxury, leaving him exhausted and on edge during the day. One of Ahmed's coping mechanisms has been avoiding anything that reminds him of the accident. He refuses to drive or even ride as a passenger, leading to strained relationships with friends who plan activities far from public transportation. His attempts at distraction through work have only led to mounting stress, creating a vicious cycle where his job performance suffers and he feels more isolated. Aisha has tried her best to support Ahmed but is growing increasingly worried about his well-being. She senses that something deeper than mere exhaustion or stress is affecting him. "You're not the same person I married," she once said during an emotional conversation, tears in her eyes. Ahmed’s response was a silent nod and an embrace filled with unspoken guilt and sorrow. Ahmed's daily routine has become fraught with small battles against his own mind. The sound of sirens passing by triggers intense anxiety, as if the same fate is about to befall him or those he loves. He often finds himself checking on Aisha and their two children unnecessarily, unable to shake off the feeling that something catastrophic could happen at any moment. The last few weeks have been particularly challenging for Ahmed. His appetite has waned, leading to noticeable weight loss, and his sleepless nights are taking a toll on his physical health. He feels trapped in a cycle of fear and avoidance, unsure how to break free from the grip of these haunting memories. Ahmed’s world is now defined by the specter of that day three years ago, an invisible force shaping every decision he makes and every moment he lives through. As he grapples with this ongoing struggle, it's clear that his life has been irrevocably altered, leaving him navigating a landscape of fear and uncertainty.
